MRI RIGHT KNEE

Clinical details: 34-year-old. Six months of anterior knee pain, worse on stairs and after prolonged sitting. No locking or instability.

Technique: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the right knee at 3T.

Comparison: Correlated with the recent radiographs.

Findings:
Menisci: Both menisci are intact. No displaced meniscal fragment.
Cruciate ligaments: The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact.
Collateral ligaments: The medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex are intact.
Extensor mechanism: The extensor mechanism is unremarkable. Patellofemoral alignment is normal.
Articular cartilage: Articular cartilage is preserved in all three compartments.
Bone marrow: No bone marrow oedema or fracture.
Joint and soft tissues: No joint effusion. No Baker's cyst. The surrounding soft tissues are unremarkable.

Impression:
1. No internal derangement of the right knee.
